revised_occurrences.paragraph: Hirt and Nichols (1981) introduced the fractional-volume basis of the volume-of-fluid method for tracking free boundaries. In the present multiphase application, material fractions also define the distribution of mobile sediment or landslide material. Geometrical interface reconstruction and a diffusive material treatment can produce different local fraction profiles. The surface diagnostic must therefore be specified along with the governing equations.

The VOF approach represents an interface through partial cell occupancy (Hirt and Nichols, 1981). The later PLIC implementation in this numerical lineage is described by Liu et al. (2005, Sect. 2.2). In a geometrical PLIC reconstruction, an interface cell contains a plane whose orientation is inferred from the fraction field and whose position is chosen to recover the specified volume. The original source treatment seeks to retain a relatively sharp interface during advection. The DBM-Diffused variant intentionally permits a different material distribution. Both treatments require a consistent diagnostic for reporting the water or sediment surface.

The model uses the laboratory-developed Splash3D framework, derived from Truchas, to solve three-dimensional incompressible flow. Finite-volume discretization is combined with volume-of-fluid tracking of the material interfaces (Hirt and Nichols, 1981). The project formulation includes large-eddy simulation with a Smagorinsky closure (Smagorinsky, 1963). The governing equations can be written as

Here u is velocity, p is pressure, ρ is mixture density, τ is the modeled stress tensor, g is gravitational acceleration, and fₘ is the volume fraction of material m. The fractional-volume interface description follows the VOF concept of Hirt and Nichols (1981). The later PLIC reconstruction is described in the Splash3D numerical lineage by Liu et al. (2005). The formulation uses a Smagorinsky-type closure, originating in Smagorinsky (1963) and given in the present three-dimensional notation by Wu et al. (2020).

A very large μ_A approximates resistance but does not set deformation identically to zero. The parameter τ₀ is the intercept of the yielded branch in this notation. It should not be conflated automatically with every definition of a measured yield stress.

Mobile sediment is represented by the discontinuous bi-viscous model, abbreviated DBM. Below the threshold rate the material has viscosity μ_A. Above it, the yielded branch has viscosity μ_B + τ₀/γ̇. The high-viscosity branch approximates strongly resistant material using a finite numerical viscosity. It permits small deformation and should not be described as an exact rigid solid. Implicit viscous treatment avoids the particularly restrictive explicit diffusion time step associated with large viscosity. The modified bi-viscosity predecessor and implicit viscous treatment are described by Wu et al. (2020); the later DBM branch definition is stated explicitly in Eq. (5) of Vuong et al. (2024). These references establish the numerical formulation, while the Guandu parameter values come from the supplied project measurements.

Deformable landslides introduce uncertainty beyond source volume and position. A material can deform, spread, and settle during motion, changing its coupling with the surrounding water. Bingham-type formulations provide a continuum description of this behavior. Three-dimensional developments within the Splash3D framework have examined rheological flows and slump-generated waves against analytical or laboratory benchmarks (Wu et al., 2020; Vuong et al., 2020). These studies motivate the use of rheology in source calculations. Their benchmark performance does not, however, establish the properties of an unobserved natural event.

Here u is velocity, p is pressure, ρ is mixture density, τ is the modeled stress tensor, g is gravitational acceleration, and fₘ is the volume fraction of material m. The fractional-volume interface description follows the VOF concept of Hirt and Nichols (1981). The later PLIC reconstruction is described in the Splash3D numerical lineage by Liu et al. (2005). The formulation uses a Smagorinsky-type closure, originating in Smagorinsky (1963) and given in the present three-dimensional notation by Wu et al. (2020).

The strain-rate invariant must be defined consistently with the stress tensor when implementing this relation. The discontinuous model permits the unyielded viscosity μ_A to be specified independently of the yielded-branch parameters. It should therefore be distinguished from a conventional bi-viscous regularization with a prescribed branch connection. Wu et al. (2020) describe this independently prescribed low-rate branch as a modified bi-viscosity model. The term DBM is used in the supplied project records; the mathematical branch definition, rather than the label, identifies the model here.

revised_occurrences.paragraph: DBM has been applied to offshore turbine foundations under waves and current (Vuong et al., 2023). Its use across geometries should not be equated with uniform quantitative accuracy. Lin et al. (2024, Sect. 3.2) report similar scour patterns around a sphere but overestimate several local depths in a sand-bed dam-break comparison. This supports reporting morphology and depth as separate assessment quantities. The forensic framework for Shuang-Yuan Bridge also links hydraulic scenarios with foundation stability (Wu et al., 2014b), rather than treating a modeled scour maximum as a complete failure criterion.

The Shuang-Yuan Bridge investigation of Wu et al. (2014b) connected reconstructed hydraulics, skewed flow, foundation conditions and structural assessment. Its relevance is the assessment sequence: a Guandu warning criterion likewise requires hydraulic and geotechnical evidence beyond the maximum erosion in one modeled case. It does not supply a transferable failure threshold.

revised_occurrences.paragraph: Xu et al. (2025) describe separate preprocessing, solver and post-processing roles in CFDAgent. In the accessible author preprint, Table 1 and Section 4.1 show the user supplying or confirming flow direction, duration, CFL and other settings. Its canonical sphere-flow checks support a particular interactive workflow, rather than unrestricted autonomous scientific diagnosis. The present Truchas workflow requires its own tests of task coverage, intervention records and preserved physical settings.

CFDAgent provides an example of language-guided preprocessing, solver execution and post-processing (Xu et al., 2025). The accessible author preprint includes explicit user choices and confirmations of numerical settings, so the relevant comparison is interactive orchestration and demonstrated task coverage. Its sphere-flow checks do not establish autonomous recovery for Truchas or DBM. A deterministic workflow baseline, conceptually comparable to explicit workflow systems (Di Tommaso et al., 2017), would help identify the benefit attributable to model-mediated decisions. That comparison remains to be performed on the recorded tasks.

revised_occurrences.paragraph: Yao et al. (2023) investigated language models that interleave reasoning and actions through external tools. This provides conceptual background for a simulation assistant that reads a task, invokes parameter-editing functions, observes logs, and decides whether to continue. The published results do not establish performance for Truchas. That performance must be assessed on the actual simulation workflow and failure set.

The architecture note describes a stateful graph with stages for intent parsing, input generation, simulation execution, diagnosis, and post-processing. Shared state contains the task specification, mesh settings, simulation status, retry count, and results. Conditional routing determines whether to continue, retry, skip a stage, or terminate. This design resembles the broader concept of interleaving model decisions with external actions discussed by Yao et al. (2023).

revised_occurrences.paragraph: The tidal versus unidirectional comparison of Yu et al. Melville and Chiew (1999) likewise identify duration dependence for clear-water cylindrical-pier scour in uniform sand.
